title: [A2 • Band 4.0] Bài 215: The Architecture of Choice: Nudge Theory
passageHtml:
PASSAGE 215 (LEVEL A2 • BAND 4.0)

The Architecture of Choice: Behavioral Nudge Theory in Public Policy

Paragraph 1. Old economic books assumed that humans always think carefully and make smart choices. In real life, people get tired, forget details, and often pick what feels easy right now. In 2008, experts Richard Thaler and Cass Sunstein explained 'nudge theory'. A nudge changes how choices are shown so the healthy or safe option feels easiest, without banning anything or charging extra taxes.

Paragraph 2. One strong tool is the automatic default choice. Because people rarely change pre-selected forms, default settings make a huge difference. In countries like Germany and the UK, citizens must sign up actively to donate organs after death, so only twelve to fifteen percent join. In Austria and Spain, citizens are listed automatically unless they say no, and over ninety-nine percent stay on the list.

Paragraph 3. Cities also use gentle nudges to protect nature. In Copenhagen, workers painted bright green footprints on sidewalks leading straight to street trash bins, cutting litter on roads by forty-six percent. In California, power companies printed simple charts on monthly bills showing how much electricity neighbours used. Many families quickly used less power to match their efficient neighbours.

Paragraph 4. Still, some thinkers worry about nudge theory. Critics say quiet nudges push people without open public discussion. They also warn that small tricks like painted sidewalks might stop leaders from solving deep social problems like poverty and climate change.

groups.title: Questions 5–8
groups.instructions: Choose the correct letter, A, B or C.

steps: Đoạn 1: "A nudge changes how choices are shown..."
Đoạn 4: "...deep social problems like poverty and climate change."

q5.text: Why do people often fail to make perfect decisions according to Paragraph 1?
options: A. Because governments forbid healthy options
B. Because people get tired and prefer easy options now
C. Because old economic books gave wrong math rules

steps: Đoạn 1: Con người hay mệt mỏi, quên chi tiết và chọn thứ dễ ngay lúc đó.

q6.text: Why are organ donor rates low in Germany and the UK?
options: A. Citizens must actively register to join the donor list.
B. Hospitals charge high fees to sign donor forms.
C. Advertising for organ donation is banned by law.

steps: Đoạn 2: Người dân phải chủ động đăng ký (sign up actively).

q7.text: What happened after California households saw neighbour power charts?
options: A. Families protested against monthly electric bills.
B. People bought new electric cars right away.
C. Families lowered their electricity use to match neighbours.

steps: Đoạn 3: Nhiều gia đình giảm dùng điện để ngang bằng hàng xóm tiết kiệm.

q8.text: What is one concern critics have about government nudges?
options: A. They are much too expensive for city budgets.
B. They influence people quietly without open debate.
C. They force citizens to pay heavy extra taxes.

steps: Đoạn 4: "...quiet nudges push people without open public discussion."
